title: ArangoDB arm64 scheduling fix on local k3d
description:
## Decision Record: ArangoDB arm64 Scheduling Fix

### Decision

Destroy and recreate the arangodb-single Pulumi local stack when the ArangoDB
operator keeps scheduling pods with amd64 affinity on an arm64 k3d cluster.

### Problem

On macOS Apple Silicon (arm64), kube-arangodb 1.2.42 creates pods with a
required node affinity for amd64, so the pod stays Pending indefinitely.

### Root Cause

The operator caches the member resolved architecture in:
  .status.members.single[0].architecture

If the ArangoDeployment was ever deployed without 'architecture: arm64'
(defaulting to amd64), that value is stored in member status. Adding
'architecture: arm64' to the spec later does NOT update it. The operator
logs 'Scheduling parameters are not updated' and keeps recreating pods
with amd64 affinity.

### Symptoms

- Pod stuck in Pending; describe shows node affinity/selector mismatch
- Pod affinity: amd64, node label: arm64
- Operator logs repeat: 'Scheduling parameters are not updated ... step=CreateMemberPodSchedulingFailurePlan'
- Member status: kubectl get arangodeployment arangodb -n dev -o jsonpath='{.status.members.single[0].architecture}' -> outputs 'amd64'

### Fix (run in order)

    # 1. Destroy — deletes ArangoDeployment, pods, and PVC (data loss OK for local)
    just local-pulumi remove-resource arangodb-single local pulumi/local-passphrase

    # 2. Recreate — operator now initialises fresh member from scratch with arm64
    just local-pulumi create-resource arangodb-single local pulumi/local-passphrase

    # 3. Verify member architecture
    KUBECONFIG=$(k3d kubeconfig write k3d-dev-cluster) \
      kubectl get arangodeployment arangodb -n dev \
      -o jsonpath='{.status.members.single[0].architecture}'
    # Must output: arm64

    # 4. Restore databases and dictycr user (PVC was wiped)
    just local-pulumi create-resource create-arangodb-databases local pulumi/local-passphrase

### Why Destroy+Recreate Works

When the operator creates a new member (no cached status), it resolves the
image manifest fresh. arangodb:3.11.6 is a multi-arch image supporting arm64.
With 'architecture: arm64' in the spec from the very first create, the operator
records the member as arm64 and schedules pods with arm64 affinity.

### What Does NOT Work

- Patching pod affinity directly: operator recreates with amd64 immediately
- Patching .status via kubectl: operator overwrites on every reconcile loop
- Pinning image to arm64 digest: operator still resolves member as amd64
- Deleting pod only: operator recreates with same amd64 affinity
close_reason: Reference document only — keep as closed knowledge base entry

title: Deploy modware-stock via Pulumi
description:
Create local Pulumi stack and deploy modware-stock to the local k3d cluster.

Setup env:
  PASSPHRASE=$(pass show pulumi/local-passphrase | head -n 1)
  export PULUMI_CONFIG_PASSPHRASE="$PASSPHRASE"
  export KUBECONFIG=$(k3d kubeconfig write k3d-dev-cluster)

Create stack:
  just local-pulumi new-stack modware-stock local pulumi/local-passphrase

Set config (use set-all pattern — one call instead of N):
  pulumi -C modware-stock config set-all --stack local --path \
      --plaintext 'modware-stock:properties.namespace=dev' \
      --plaintext 'modware-stock:properties.appName=stock' \
      --plaintext 'modware-stock:properties.port=9345' \
      --plaintext 'modware-stock:properties.logLevel=debug' \
      --plaintext 'modware-stock:properties.command=start-server' \
      --plaintext 'modware-stock:properties.image.name=dictybase/modware-stock' \
      --plaintext 'modware-stock:properties.image.tag=develop-2985bd5' \
      --plaintext 'modware-stock:properties.arangodbSecret.name=backend' \
      --plaintext 'modware-stock:properties.arangodbSecret.userkey=user' \
      --plaintext 'modware-stock:properties.arangodbSecret.passkey=password'

Deploy:
  just local-pulumi create-resource modware-stock local pulumi/local-passphrase

Note: key names use lowercase 'userkey'/'passkey' (differs from modware-annotation which uses capital K).
close_reason: Deployed modware-stock via Pulumi to k3d. Image ghcr.io/dictybase/modware-stock:92ec242. Fixed arm64 ArangoDB scheduling by destroying and recreating arangodb-single stack so operator initializes member fresh with architecture:arm64.

comments.author: Siddhartha Basu
comments.text:
## Deployment Plan

### Image
- Registry: ghcr.io/dictybase/modware-stock
- Tag: 92ec242
- Full ref: ghcr.io/dictybase/modware-stock:92ec242

### Step 1 — Environment Setup
```bash
PASSPHRASE=$(pass show pulumi/local-passphrase | head -n 1)
export PULUMI_CONFIG_PASSPHRASE="$PASSPHRASE"
export KUBECONFIG=$(k3d kubeconfig write k3d-dev-cluster)
```

### Step 2 — Create Local Stack
```bash
just local-pulumi new-stack modware-stock local pulumi/local-passphrase
```
This initialises a passphrase-encrypted local stack and creates Pulumi.local.yaml in the modware-stock directory.

### Step 3 — Configure the Stack
Key differences from the issue template:
- image.name changed to ghcr.io/dictybase/modware-stock
- image.tag changed to 92ec242
- arangodbSecret keys use lowercase userkey/passkey (as noted in the issue)

```bash
pulumi -C modware-stock config set-all --stack local --path \
    --plaintext 'modware-stock:properties.namespace=dev' \
    --plaintext 'modware-stock:properties.appName=stock' \
    --plaintext 'modware-stock:properties.port=9345' \
    --plaintext 'modware-stock:properties.logLevel=debug' \
    --plaintext 'modware-stock:properties.command=start-server' \
    --plaintext 'modware-stock:properties.image.name=ghcr.io/dictybase/modware-stock' \
    --plaintext 'modware-stock:properties.image.tag=92ec242' \
    --plaintext 'modware-stock:properties.arangodbSecret.name=backend' \
    --plaintext 'modware-stock:properties.arangodbSecret.userkey=user' \
    --plaintext 'modware-stock:properties.arangodbSecret.passkey=password'
```

### Step 4 — Deploy
```bash
just local-pulumi create-resource modware-stock local pulumi/local-passphrase
```

### Expected Kubernetes Resources
The backend.go program creates:
- Deployment: stock-api-server (1 replica, namespace dev)
  - Container image: ghcr.io/dictybase/modware-stock:92ec242
  - Env: ARANGODB_USER and ARANGODB_PASSWORD from secret 'backend'
  - Args: --log-level debug start-server --user $(ARANGODB_USER) --pass $(ARANGODB_PASSWORD) --port 9345
- Service: stock-api (ClusterIP, port 9345, namespace dev)

### Notes
- KUBECONFIG must point to k3d-dev-cluster throughout; do not switch global context
- Pulumi local backend state is stored in pulumi-files/local-state
- The Pulumi.local.yaml will use encryptionsalt (passphrase-based, not GCP KMS like experiments stack)

comments.author: Siddhartha Basu
comments.text:
## Plan: Deploy NATS to Local k3d Cluster

### Approach
Create a local Pulumi stack for the existing `nats/` Pulumi program (Helm-based).
No code changes needed — only stack config and deployment.

### Config (local stack vs experiments)
| Key | Experiments | Local |
|-----|-------------|-------|
| storage.class | dictycr-balanced | local-path |
| storage.size | 20Gi | 1Gi |
| chart.name | nats | nats |
| chart.version | 1.2.4 | 1.2.4 |
| image.tag | 2.10.20-alpine | 2.10.20-alpine |
| namespace | dev | dev |

### Steps
1. Create local stack: `just local-pulumi new-stack nats local pulumi/local-passphrase`
2. Set config:
```
pulumi -C nats config set-all --stack local --path \
    --plaintext 'nats:properties.namespace=dev' \
    --plaintext 'nats:properties.chart.name=nats' \
    --plaintext 'nats:properties.chart.repository=https://nats-io.github.io/k8s/helm/charts' \
    --plaintext 'nats:properties.chart.version=1.2.4' \
    --plaintext 'nats:properties.image.tag=2.10.20-alpine' \
    --plaintext 'nats:properties.storage.class=local-path' \
    --plaintext 'nats:properties.storage.size=1Gi'
```
3. Deploy: `just local-pulumi create-resource nats local pulumi/local-passphrase`

### Verification
```
kubectl -n dev get pods -l app.kubernetes.io/name=nats
kubectl -n dev get svc nats
```
Expected: pod Running, service nats on port 4222.

title: Upgrade ArangoDB operator from 1.2.42 to 1.3.4
description:
Current version: 1.2.42 (arangodb/kube-arangodb:1.2.42)
Target version: 1.3.4 (two below latest 1.4.1)

Installed via Pulumi + Helm release (arangodb-operator/main.go).
Version is controlled by arangodb-operator/Pulumi.local.yaml.

PLAN

Step 1 — Edit arangodb-operator/Pulumi.local.yaml
  Change both version fields from 1.2.42 to 1.3.4:
  - arangodb-operator:chart.version
  - arangodb-operator:properties.chart.version

Step 2 — Run Pulumi update
  export KUBECONFIG=$(k3d kubeconfig write k3d-dev-cluster)
  just local-pulumi create-resource arangodb-operator local pulumi/local-passphrase
  (Triggers Helm upgrade in-place; operator pod restarts with new image)

Step 3 — Verify
  KUBECONFIG=$(k3d kubeconfig write k3d-dev-cluster) \
    kubectl get deployment -n dev arango-arangodb-operator-29dc600f-operator \
    -o jsonpath='{.spec.template.spec.containers[0].image}'
  Expected: arangodb/kube-arangodb:1.3.4

Release notes: https://github.com/arangodb/kube-arangodb/releases/tag/1.3.4
notes: Verified cluster access method: Use 'export KUBECONFIG=$(k3d kubeconfig write k3d-dev-cluster)' to target the local k3d cluster.

comments.author: Siddhartha Basu
comments.text:
## Detailed Upgrade Plan: ArangoDB Operator 1.2.42 → 1.3.4

### Context

The ArangoDB operator is deployed to the local `k3d-dev-cluster` via Pulumi + Helm. The Pulumi program lives in `arangodb-operator/main.go` and reads config from `arangodb-operator/Pulumi.local.yaml`. The version string appears in two places in that YAML file — both must be updated.

---

### Step 1 — Edit `arangodb-operator/Pulumi.local.yaml`

Change both occurrences of `1.2.42` → `1.3.4`:

```yaml
# arangodb-operator:chart.version
version: 1.3.4

# arangodb-operator:properties.chart.version
version: 1.3.4
```

Diff:
```diff
-    version: 1.2.42
+    version: 1.3.4
 ...
-      version: 1.2.42
+      version: 1.3.4
```

---

### Step 2 — Set KUBECONFIG to target the local k3d cluster

```bash
export KUBECONFIG=$(k3d kubeconfig write k3d-dev-cluster)
```

---

### Step 3 — Run Pulumi upgrade

```bash
just local-pulumi create-resource arangodb-operator local pulumi/local-passphrase
```

What this does internally:
1. Fetches the passphrase from `pass show pulumi/local-passphrase`
2. Sets `PULUMI_CONFIG_PASSPHRASE`
3. Runs `pulumi -C arangodb-operator up -s local -f -y`
4. Pulumi detects the chart version diff, performs a `helm upgrade` of the `kube-arangodb` chart
5. Operator deployment rolls out a new pod with image `arangodb/kube-arangodb:1.3.4`

---

### Step 4 — Verify the upgrade

```bash
KUBECONFIG=$(k3d kubeconfig write k3d-dev-cluster) \
  kubectl get deployment -n dev arango-arangodb-operator-29dc600f-operator \
  -o jsonpath='{.spec.template.spec.containers[0].image}'
```

Expected output: `arangodb/kube-arangodb:1.3.4`

Confirm rollout:
```bash
KUBECONFIG=$(k3d kubeconfig write k3d-dev-cluster) \
  kubectl rollout status deployment/arango-arangodb-operator-29dc600f-operator -n dev
```

---

### Step 5 — Commit and close

```bash
/ai-commit-gen:commit
bd close cluster-ops-d7r --reason="Upgraded ArangoDB operator to 1.3.4 via Pulumi Helm upgrade"
bd sync
git push
```

---

### Risk / Notes

| Risk | Mitigation |
|------|-----------|
| CRD schema changes between 1.2.x → 1.3.x | kube-arangodb Helm chart handles CRD upgrades automatically on helm upgrade |
| Operator pod restart causes brief control-plane gap | Existing ArangoDeployment resources continue running; only new reconciliations pause briefly |
| Passphrase not in pass store | Run `pass show pulumi/local-passphrase` first to confirm it exists |
| k3d cluster not running | Run `k3d cluster list` to confirm k3d-dev-cluster is up |

title: Restore arangodump databases into ArangoDB
description:
Port-forward to ArangoDB then run arangorestore to load all databases from scratch/arangodump/ into the local k3d instance.

Steps:
1. kubectl port-forward -n dev service/arangodb-single-diejsnkq 8529:8529
2. ROOT_PASS=$(pass show arangodb/local-root | head -n 1)
3. docker run --rm --net=host -v "${PWD}/scratch/arangodump:/dump" arangodb/arangodb:3.11.6 arangorestore --server.endpoint tcp://127.0.0.1:8529 --server.username root --server.password "$ROOT_PASS" --input-directory /dump --all-databases true --create-database true

Databases to restore: _system, annofeature, annotation, cgm_ddb, chado, content, order, stock
Skip: lost+found (filesystem artifact)

Restore _system first to set up ArangoDB system collections.
close_reason: Databases restored via just arangodb restore-local-arangodb. All 8 DBs present: _system, annofeature, annotation, cgm_ddb, chado, content, order, stock.
